[#hash-kdfs-compare]
.What each of "Key derivation" is
[cols="2,1,3,2,1,2",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Output | Security | Standard | Status | In the browser (WebCrypto)

| <<hash-hkdf,`hkdf_extract`>>
| the hmac's digest size
| that of the hmac, given input with enough entropy
| RFC 5869
| recommended
| HKDF (whole only)

| <<hash-hkdf,`hkdf_expand`>>
| 1 to 255 times the digest size
| that of the hmac
| RFC 5869
| recommended
| HKDF (whole only)

| <<hash-hkdf,`hkdf`>>
| 1 to 255 times the digest size
| that of the hmac, given input with enough entropy
| RFC 5869
| recommended
| HKDF

| <<hash-pbkdf2,`pbkdf2`>>
| 1 to (2^32 - 1) times the digest size
| each guess costs the iterations; no defence against GPUs beyond that
| RFC 8018
| where a standard names it
| PBKDF2

| <<hash-blake2b-subkey,`blake2b_subkey`>>
| 16 to 64 bytes
| that of the master key, which must be 32 uniformly random bytes; at most the subkey's length
| libsodium's crypto_kdf: keyed BLAKE2b (RFC 7693) with the subkey's id as the salt and the context as the personalisation
| recommended
| no
|===

[#hash-kdfs-choose]
.How to choose among "Key derivation"
[cols="2,2,2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Fastest natively | Smallest on Emscripten | Where it is used | Choose it when

| <<hash-hkdf,`hkdf_extract`>>
| 480 ns (sodium)
| 17,499 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/44.md[NIP-44's conversation key]; link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-7.1[TLS 1.3's key schedule]
| When a protocol names the extract step alone.

| <<hash-hkdf,`hkdf_expand`>>
| 489 ns (sodium)
| 24,778 bytes (sodium)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-7.1[TLS 1.3's key schedule]; link:https://signal.org/docs/specifications/doubleratchet/[Signal's Double Ratchet]
| Keys from a key that is already uniform (a master key), one per info label.

| <<hash-hkdf,`hkdf`>>
| 980 ns (sodium)
| 23,281 bytes (bearssl)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-7.1[TLS 1.3]; link:https://signal.org/docs/specifications/doubleratchet/[Signal's protocols]; link:https://www.wireguard.com/protocol/[WireGuard (over HMAC-BLAKE2s)]
| The default way to turn one secret into several keys. Never for passwords.

| <<hash-pbkdf2,`pbkdf2`>>
| 6.1 ms (openssl)
| 29,235 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0039.mediawiki[BIP39's seeds (2,048 iterations of HMAC-SHA-512)]; link:https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html[OWASP: 600,000 iterations of HMAC-SHA-256 for passwords]
| When a standard or FIPS 140 demands it; otherwise Argon2id for passwords.

| <<hash-blake2b-subkey,`blake2b_subkey`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://doc.libsodium.org/key_derivation[libsodium's key derivation, crypto_kdf_derive_from_key]
| To derive the keys a libsodium program derives from the same master key, or keys numbered by id from one random master key; hkdf for a secret that is not uniformly random.
|===

The measured columns are doc/measurements.json's, a reference measured on 2026-11-16 on Apple M5 Max that decides nothing: the native throughput over 1 MiB, or the time of one derivation over `hmac_sha2_256`, of the fastest backend, and the smallest Emscripten program that calls the function; <<hash-measurements>> has every backend on every target.
